title: The Sun and Other Stars
seo_title: Grade 5 Sun and Stars Worksheets: Why the Sun Looks Brighter, Distance and Light-Years
standard_text: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from Earth.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on the sun and other stars (NGSS 5-ESS1-1): the sun is a star, distance and apparent brightness, light-years, and flashlight models. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: The sun looks brightest because it is the closest star.
key_sub: The same light looks dimmer from farther away. Other stars look like faint dots only because they are so far from Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

The sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth, about 150 million kilometers away. The next closest star is more than 4 light-years away, about 270,000 times farther.

How bright a light looks depends on how far away it is. The same light looks dimmer from farther away, because the light spreads out before it reaches your eyes. That is why the sun looks so much brighter and bigger than the other stars.

Example

Two identical stars are 10 and 50 light-years away. Which looks brighter?

They give off the same light.

The closer one looks brighter.

Answer: the one 10 light-years away

Example

Why can't we see stars in the daytime?

Stars are always shining.

The sun's light fills the sky and hides their dim light.

Answer: The sunlight outshines them.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the sun is not a star. It is a star that is very close.
  • Thinking the brightest-looking star gives off the most light. Distance matters too.
  • Thinking stars disappear in the daytime. Sunlight hides them.
  • Thinking a light-year is a time. It is a distance.

faq.a: Yes. The sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth.

faq.q: Why does the sun look brighter than other stars?
faq.a: Because it is much closer. Light looks dimmer the farther it travels, and other stars are hundreds of thousands of times farther away.
The distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers. It measures distance, not time.

faq.q: Why can't we see stars during the day?
faq.a: The stars are still shining, but the sun's bright light fills the sky and hides their dimmer light.

items.q: Light from the sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. Light from Proxima Centauri takes 4.2 years. Why does the sun look so much brighter?
c: The sun is much, much closer to Earth.
The sun is the biggest star in the universe.
The sun is the only star that gives off light.
Proxima Centauri is a planet, not a star.
items.e: The sun is about 8 light-minutes away; Proxima Centauri is 4.2 light-years away. Distance makes the difference.

items.q: Why does the sun look much brighter than other stars?
c: Other stars are turned off in the day.
It is the only star that gives off light.
It is much closer to Earth than any other star.
items.e: The sun is about 150 million km away. The next closest star is about 270,000 times farther.

items.q: A star looks very dim from Earth. Which could be true?
c: It must not give off light.
It may be very far away.
It must be smaller than a house.
items.e: Distance can make even a very bright star look dim.

items.q: How does distance change how bright a light looks?
c: Lights look brightest from very far away.
The farther away, the brighter it looks.
The farther away, the dimmer it looks.
items.e: Light spreads out as it travels, so less reaches your eyes from far away.

items.q: A streetlight looks bright up close but dim from a mile away. How is this like stars?
c: Stars look dim because they are very far away.
Stars get turned down at night.
items.e: The same light looks dimmer from farther away.

items.q: Which statement about stars is true?
c: Many stars are as big as or bigger than the sun.
Stars are holes in the sky.
All stars are smaller than Earth.
Stars are closer than the moon.
items.e: Stars look like tiny dots only because they are so far away.

items.q: Why can't we see stars during the day?
c: Stars move away during the day.
The sun's bright light hides their dimmer light.
items.e: The stars are still there. Sunlight scattered in the sky outshines them.

items.q: Which object in the sky is a star?
items.e: The moon and planets reflect sunlight. The sun makes its own light.
